title: SLOWPULSE_Backdoor_Investigation_79d
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a suspected compromise involving the SLOWPULSE backdoor malware on a Pulse Secure VPN appliance. The malware is known to maintain persistence, facilitate lateral movement, and exfiltrate data. Your mission is to identify and mitigate the threat.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a suspected compromise involving the SLOWPULSE backdoor malware on a Pulse Secure VPN appliance. The malware is known to maintain persistence, facilitate lateral movement, and exfiltrate data. Your mission is to identify and mitigate the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the network, you noticed unusual outbound connections from the target host. Investigate the running services on the target host to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services.
levels.solution: To identify suspicious services, you can use the `systemctl list-units --type=service` command to list all running services. Look for any services that seem out of place or unfamiliar. The suspicious service in this scenario is the `bkd.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the list of running services and look for any that seem out of place or unfamiliar.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `systemctl list-units --type=service` command to list all running services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious service is not a standard system service and is likely related to the malware.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: Now that you have identified a suspicious service, determine how it is automatically started after a system reboot. This will help you understand the persistence mechanism used by the malware.
levels.solution: To determine the persistence mechanism, you can use the `systemctl list-unit-files` command to list all systemd unit files. Look for any unit files related to the suspicious service. The persistence mechanism in this scenario is the `bkd.service` unit file.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate systemd services and timers to find any related to the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `systemctl list-unit-files` command to list all systemd unit files.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The persistence mechanism is likely a systemd unit file that starts the suspicious service.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: The suspicious service appears to be communicating with an external command-and-control server. Determine which network port is used for this communication to help contain the threat.
levels.solution: To determine the network port used for C2 communication, you can use the `ss -tulnp` command to list all listening ports. Look for any ports that seem suspicious. The C2 port number in this scenario is 4444.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Analyze network connections and listen ports to identify the suspicious port.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `ss -tulnp` command to list all listening ports.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious port is likely a non-standard port used by the malware for C2 communication.
